verdict.rationale: Homebrew's own docs describe a central registry: homebrew-core formulae with prebuilt bottles, casks for upstream apps, fonts and plugins, a JSON API listing every core formula and cask, and third-party taps for anything else, across macOS, Linux and WSL. Community reports back this up, saying it has many more packages than MacPorts, seems better maintained than Nix, and auto-bumps recipes so new releases ship within hours. missing for 10: no quantitative registry-size evidence, and some users report version lag on specific packages (Elixir, llama.cpp) and no standard multi-version installs for node, php and Python.
